title: Deprecation Bridge and Customer Migration Accelerator for StreamAdapters
creator: Aisha Kapoor
description: Goal: Remove the aging StreamAdapter V0 transport while giving customers a low-friction migration path. Deliver a short-lived deprecation bridge (compat shim) plus a Migration Accelerator: a CLI tool and SDK helpers that rewrite legacy requests, collect migration telemetry, and provide automated client snippets. This ticket defines scope, acceptance criteria, rollout phases, and instrumentation needed to safely retire the old transport with minimal customer disruption.
business_justification: Unified inference API reduces maintenance cost, simplifies routing and observability, and enables newer features (structured outputs, function/tool-calling). Removing StreamAdapter V0 eliminates a brittle compatibility layer that complicates scaling and kernel selection.
requirements: Provide a lightweight compat shim (deprecation bridge) that accepts legacy requests and translates them to unified API for a limited grace period (90 days).
Publish Migration Accelerator: CLI tool with --rewrite, --dry-run, and --telemetry flags and language SDK helpers (Node/Python) that detect and rewrite legacy payloads to new schema.
Instrument migration events: success/failure, error types, per-customer migration progress, and traffic split to be visible in Console.
Add versioned deprecation banners to Console and to API responses (warning headers) for customers calling affected endpoints.
Define rollout gating criteria tied to telemetry (error rates, % migrated) with automatic rollback criteria.
Create runbooks for SRE and Support for common migration failures and troubleshooting steps.
acceptance_criteria: Compat shim deployed in a segregated pool with traffic limits and feature-flagged routing to prevent overload.
Migration Accelerator v1 released (CLI + Node + Python helpers) with published docs and example PRs; sample project that rewrites at least 3 common legacy patterns.
Telemetry: dashboard showing per-customer migration % and error classification; alerts created for shim error rate > 1% or CPU saturation on shim nodes.
At least 3 enterprise customers complete an opt-in migration pilot and report no functional regressions; pilot logs and postmortem artifacts captured.
Deactivation playbook and rollback criteria reviewed and approved by SRE, Security, and Legal.
rollout_timeline: Phase 0 (internal): 2025-03-10 to 2025-03-24 – build prototypical shim, CLI alpha, and telemetry plumbing; run internal migration of infra teams.
Phase 1 (beta customers): 2025-04-01 to 2025-05-01 – opt-in beta for 10 customers with dedicated support; iterate on CLI and SDK fixes.
Phase 2 (public opt-in): 2025-05-05 to 2025-06-05 – publicly announced opt-in with migration guides, SDKs, and webinars; Monitor metrics and adjust quotas.
Phase 3 (forced deprecation): 2025-06-20 – disable write access to StreamAdapter V0; provide read-only grace for exports until 2025-07-20; full removal afterwards.
migration_playbook: Step 1: Identify requests using affected endpoints (Console query + telemetry).
Step 2: Run Migration Accelerator in dry-run mode to surface rewrite diffs and flag incompatibilities.
Step 3: Coordinate schema fixes (prompts/metadata) with customer engineers; provide patch snippets via Support playbook.
Step 4: Enable automatic rewrite (--rewrite) behind customer toggle for 7-day trial.
Step 5: Confirm behavior parity via regression prompt set and monitoring traces.
Step 6: Flip routing to unified API and retire legacy traffic; close the ticket when customer confirms.
communication_plan: Week -6: Private notice to customers with active use (email + account teams) and invite to pilot.
Week -4: Publish Migration Guide in Docs and announce SDK releases with examples in Release Notes.
Week -2: Host live webinar and office hours; publish FAQ and automated support playbook for field teams.
Ongoing: In-Console banners, header warnings on affected endpoints, and targeted in-app recommendations for high-usage customers.
risks_and_mitigation: Risk: Compat shim could become traffic hotspot -> Mitigation: Place shim in a bounded pool, use strict rate limits and per-customer quotas.
Risk: Rewrites may alter semantics for edge-case prompts -> Mitigation: Provide dry-run diff, regression test harness, and manual review process for flagged rewrites.
Risk: Customers ignore opt-in -> Mitigation: Account outreach, in-console guidance, limited-time auto-rewrite option, and staggered enforcement.
sre_and_security_notes: Shim services must run in customer-isolated subnets for enterprise customers where required.
All rewrite logs must strip PII and follow retention policy; KMS-integrated logging for enterprise pilots.
Security review completed 2025-02-28; outstanding follow-up: confirm HSM usage for enterprise export flows.
notes_and_updates: 2025-02-13: Kickoff with Eng, SRE, Design. Agreed scope: shim + CLI + SDK helpers, no long-term compat maintenance.
2025-02-20: Design review – Mei suggested sample UI flow for in-console migration toggle; accepted with minor changes.
2025-02-25: Security review flagged log retention and HSM requirement for exports; assigned follow-up to Eng (ENG-3102).
2025-03-01: SRE proposed segregated pool + circuit breaker; added to acceptance criteria and rollout gating.
2025-03-04: PM approved external comms timeline; scheduled webinar for 2025-04-08.
qa_strategy: Create a canonical legacy->unified request corpus with 500+ test cases derived from production logs (sanitized).
Automated end-to-end tests: CLI dry-run vs live rewrite, SDK unit tests for helpers, integration tests against shim in staging.
Define success metrics and attach to CI pipeline: zero regressions on core prompt set and <0.5% functional diffs for edge prompts.
